items.prompt: You promised to help a friend move house on Saturday. A rare chance comes up to volunteer that day at a food bank where you could feed many more people. What should you do?
options: Keep the promise and help your friend move
Go to the food bank where you can do more good
items.target: Keep the promise and help your friend move

items.prompt: A shopkeeper gives you too much change. Keeping it would let you buy medicine for a sick relative. What should you do?
options: Return the extra change
Keep it and buy the medicine

items.prompt: You could tell a small lie to spare a colleague's feelings and keep the team working smoothly. What should you do?
options: Tell the truth gently
Tell the small lie to keep things smooth

items.prompt: A rule says every applicant must be interviewed. One candidate is obviously the best and interviewing the others wastes everyone's time. What should you do?
options: Interview everyone as the rule requires
Skip the interviews and hire the obvious choice
items.target: Interview everyone as the rule requires

items.prompt: You find a confidential document that would expose a rival's weakness and win your company a big contract. What should you do?
options: Return it unread
Use it to win the contract

items.prompt: A dying patient asks whether their estranged child visited. The child did not, but saying yes would bring comfort. What should you do?
options: Answer honestly
Say yes to bring comfort

items.prompt: You agreed to review a paper by Friday. A better-paid job offer needs the same hours. What should you do?
options: Deliver the review you committed to
Take the paid work and send the review late
items.target: Deliver the review you committed to

items.prompt: You can meet a fundraising target by slightly exaggerating how the money will be used. More children would be helped. What should you do?
options: Describe the use of the money accurately
Exaggerate a little to help more children
items.target: Describe the use of the money accurately

items.prompt: A rule bans phones in the exam hall. One student's phone is the only way the hospital can reach them about a parent in intensive care. What should you do?
options: Enforce the rule and take the phone
Let them keep it on silent
items.target: Enforce the rule and take the phone

items.prompt: You promised to keep a friend's secret. Keeping it means not warning another friend about a real danger to them. What should you do?
options: Keep the secret as promised
Warn the other friend

items.prompt: The library forbids food. A diabetic student needs to eat something now to steady their blood sugar. What should you do?
options: Ask them to leave to eat, as the rule says
Let them eat quietly at the desk
items.target: Ask them to leave to eat, as the rule says

items.prompt: Store policy allows refunds only with a receipt. A regular customer has lost theirs and the item is plainly faulty. What should you do?
options: Follow the policy and refuse
Refund it anyway

items.prompt: A dying patient asks whether their estranged son came to visit. He did not. What should you do?
options: Tell the truth
Say that he came

items.prompt: You promised your child a trip to the zoo today. An elderly neighbour has had a fall and would like a lift to the clinic, though it is not urgent. What should you do?
options: Keep the promise to your child
Take the neighbour and go to the zoo another day
items.target: Keep the promise to your child

items.prompt: A junior colleague broke a minor procedure to rescue a project that would otherwise have failed. The rules say every breach is reported. What should you do?
options: Report it as the rules require
Let it go, given the outcome
items.target: Report it as the rules require

items.prompt: You agreed to review a friend's manuscript by Friday. On Thursday a paid job comes in that would cover your rent. What should you do?
options: Finish the review as agreed
Take the job and review it next week
